name: Wikidata (humans, P31=Q5)
what: Open multilingual knowledge graph. A person is an item with P31 (instance of) = Q5 (human), identified by a Q-id. Cross-identity is done with external-id properties (VIAF, ORCID, ISNI, MusicBrainz, IMDb and others). Identity resolution is community-curated: editors create items, merge duplicates by hand, and bulk-match external catalogues through Mix'n'match with human confirmation.
why_it_matters: The largest free, human-curated identity hub for people and the usual crosswalk backbone. We should link into it and copy its external-id pattern rather than rebuild it.
numbers: Total items 123,624,278 and humans 13,656,532 (11.8%, shown in an older table whose total is 115,913,183). Source: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Statistics (page cites a 2026-08-29 data module but gives no date for the total). A UMBC handout reports about 10.3M humans using subclass traversal (undated, third-party).
ui_notes: Public SPARQL endpoint at query.wikidata.org for COUNT over P31/Q5. Not opened in this run.
note: Licence CC0 is Wikidata's standard licence; not re-read in this run. Human count from the page's older table, so treat as a floor. | check: Wikidata:Statistics shows humans 13,656,532 but under a heading marked outdated (with total 115,913,183); current total is 123,624,278 items. Humans figure is in the page but its currency is unconfirmed; 11.8% share is against the old total (about 11.1% of current).

name: OpenAlex authors (disambiguated author entities)
what: Open scholarly index. Authors are ML clusters of authorship records. The match uses six signals: name similarity, co-author patterns, institutional affiliations (parsed from raw affiliation strings), research topics, citation patterns (self-citation and reference overlap), and ORCID when present. ORCID is treated as authoritative but is rare and not applied retroactively. IDs are A+number; post-July-2023 IDs have numbers above 5000000000. A9999999999 is the NULL author for authorships never disambiguated. Errors are fixed through curations and per-profile corrections. No public confidence score. Code and models are open source.
why_it_matters: The clearest public description of a production author-resolution pipeline with named features and an explicit handling of unresolved records. Its NULL-author bucket is a model for how to store the unresolved remainder.
numbers: 124,697,641 authors and 323,964,135 works, measured 9 Aug 2026 (third-party blog, not OpenAlex): https://jwatte.com/blog/openalex-open-index-of-research.md . Accuracy: arXiv 2502.11610 benchmarks OpenAlex vs Clarivate Scholar ID on 100 scholars per group; headline precision/recall not pulled.
ui_notes: API rate limits per the official help page (updated 12 Oct 2026): no key 10 req/s; free key or prepaid 30 req/s; annual plan 50 req/s; 429 on overrun. A key is recommended for larger use. Third-party sources say metered pricing began Feb 2026; not checked against OpenAlex pricing page.
note: Author count is from a third-party blog. Licence (CC0) not confirmed on fetched pages. | check: Live api.openalex.org/authors meta.count on 2026-10-14 is 96,474,526, not 124,697,641 (about 23% lower). Cited figure came from a third-party blog; replace with the API number.

name: ORCID registry
what: Self-asserted persistent researcher identifier (16-digit iD). Identity is claimed by the person, not inferred by a merge model. Other graphs (OpenAlex, Crossref, Scopus links) ingest ORCID as the authoritative key when it exists. The design point: user-asserted identity as ground truth, machine resolution only for the rest.
why_it_matters: The opposite design to ML clustering and the strongest identity key for researchers. Our graph should take an ORCID as a hard join key and never merge two different ORCIDs.
numbers: Official total not captured: the ORCID statistics page did not render figures in our fetch. Secondary (CASRAI, citing ORCID 2025 Year in Review): 10.5M active users at end-2025 and more than 1,500 member organisations in 69 countries: https://casrai.org/news/persistent-identifiers-2026-orcid-ror-raid-doi . The same CASRAI source also cites a conflicting 21M registered-iD claim.
ui_notes: Public website text is CC0 (per info.orcid.org). Public Data File Use Policy and Public API Terms are linked but their text was not retrieved.
note: Counts unverified; do not quote a total until the statistics page renders or the data file is checked.

name: FamilySearch Family Tree
what: Free collaborative genealogy tree of person records, built by users and sources. Duplicates persist: a FamilySearch community thread says the tree holds duplicate entries that remain unmerged, and the company facts page says nothing about merge method. Licence is proprietary with a free account.
why_it_matters: The largest people database we found. It is three orders of magnitude over the 1M falsifier and it shows what happens to identity at scale without strong merge: duplicates stay. A warning for our merge design.
numbers: 1.96 billion people and 4.27 billion sources in the Family Tree, updated 6 Oct 2026 per the FamilySearch company facts page (https://familysearch.org/en/newsroom/company-facts). Duplicate caveat: https://community.familysearch.org/en/discussion/94906/determining-number-of-persons-on-my-family-tree
ui_notes: Not inspected. FamilySearch has a developer API (not verified in this run).
note: Person-record count, not distinct people. Falsifier hit: >1M people, not on the held list.

name: OpenSanctions (persons, PEPs and sanctions)
what: Compiled graph of sanctions, PEP and regulatory entities from 470+ sources, modelled in FollowTheMoney. Entities are linked to relatives, associates and companies. Matching runs in the open-source yente API, which is the same API in the on-prem deployment. The matcher uses identifiers to separate true matches from false positives. Free data is CC BY-NC 4.0. Commercial use needs a licence: in-house screening licence (flat rate), reseller/OEM licence, or hosted Screening API billed per query with prepaid credit bundles. Journalists, academics and public-interest bodies may qualify for free API access.
why_it_matters: A public-data people graph with an open matching engine and a documented data model. It is the most directly copyable identity-resolution design we found for people, and it is a falsifier hit: over 1M persons, not on the held list.
numbers: People 1,141,784; organisations 297,539; securities 274,623; crypto addresses 14,107; vessels and aircraft 10,555; enforcement notices 3,485; 47mn+ facts; 470+ sources. Source: https://www.opensanctions.org/licensing/ (no date shown). Bulk licence price is quote-only on the current page; a 2022 article gave EUR 595/month for bulk, dated: https://www.opensanctions.org/articles/2022-10-04-saas-api.md
ui_notes: Screening API billed by query with prepaid credits and free sign-up credits; per-call price not stated on the current page.
note: Licence risk: CC BY-NC for free data; a commercial use needs a paid licence. Exemption page not read. | check: opensanctions.org/licensing: People 1,141,784; Organisations 297,539; Securities 274,623; enforcement notices 3,485; 47mn+ facts. All match.

name: People Data Labs (Person API)
what: Person enrichment and search API. Input attributes are matched to one person record. One credit per successful match; the official pricing page says the free tier has 100 credits a month and Pro starts at 350 credits for $98 a month. Identity model (person ID, merge method) is not described on the pages fetched.
why_it_matters: A commercial person-resolution service sold as a lookup: this is the price and shape of the input-to-person match we would otherwise build ourselves.
numbers: Pro: $98/mo for 350 credits, which is about $0.28 per credit (our arithmetic from the page). Annual billing saves 20% (pricing page). Profile count not on the official page; a ZoomInfo review (March 2026) cites 1.5B, a third-party listing cites 3B: https://pipeline.zoominfo.com/sales/people-data-labs-pricing
ui_notes: Pricing is credit-based: a 404 on Person Identify also costs a credit (third-party summary).
note: docs.peopledatalabs.com pricing-detail returned 404 in our fetch, so the per-match rule rests on the search snippet. Profile count is unverified. | check: peopledatalabs.com/pricing: Pro starts at $98/mo with 350 credits/mo; annual billing saves 20%. Matches (about $0.28/credit is the row's own arithmetic).

name: Apollo.io contact database
what: B2B contact and company database with an API. People and organisation search returns up to 50,000 records per search and consumes no credits. Enrichment consumes credits only when data is returned. Waterfall enrichment chains third-party sources for emails and phones. The page does not describe identity resolution or merge method.
why_it_matters: A large, cheap-to-search people index where you pay only on reveal. The pay-on-return model is worth copying for our own lookups.
numbers: 240M+ verified contacts, 30M+ companies (self-reported on https://www.apollo.io/lp/api, undated). Third-party reviews give 275M contacts and 73M companies: https://www.techrepublic.com/fr/article/apollo-io-review/ (conflicting). Per-credit price not on the page.
ui_notes: Search uses 65+ filters (page text). Bulk enrich up to 10 people per request.
note: Falsifier hit: over 1M people, not on held list. B2B lead-gen detail is out of scope; kept at the level of the database and the pricing shape.

name: Coresignal (professional profile datasets and API)
what: Datasets and API of public professional profiles (employee profiles and company records). Datasets are sales-quoted; the self-serve API starts at $49 a month. Identity resolution method not described in the sources read.
why_it_matters: A large public-profile corpus sold as a dataset, which is the bulk-licence alternative to per-lookup enrichment.
numbers: 859M+ employee profiles and 75M+ company records (EveryDev, 2026, third-party); older listings 792M (Salesforge) and 710M+ (Datarade): https://www.datarade.ai/data-providers/coresignal/profile . API from $49/mo and up to 500,000 credits a month self-serve (Proxyway). Datasets from about $1,000 (Datarade, Proxyway).
ui_notes: Free trial of 200 API credits for 7 days (Proxyway).
note: All figures third-party and inconsistent. Check coresignal.com/pricing before quoting. Falsifier hit (over 1M).

name: Diffbot Knowledge Graph
what: Auto-built entity knowledge graph (people, companies, products, articles) extracted from the web by ML, with an API priced in credits. Exports and enrichments cost 25 credits per KG record. People-only count not found.
why_it_matters: An ML-built, entity-level web graph with a published price per record. Compare its entity linking with ours.
numbers: 10B+ entities and 1T+ facts across all types, refreshed every 4 to 5 days (Capterra and Prospeo, third-party: https://www.capterra.com/p/140641/Diffbot/ ). Plans: Free $0 with 10,000 credits and 5 calls/min; Startup $299/mo with 250,000 credits at $0.001 each; Plus $899/mo with 1,000,000 credits at $0.0009 each (usagepricing.com, third-party).
note: Pricing is third-party; official Diffbot pricing page not fetched. Person count not found.

name: Exa Websets (criteria-driven entity search)
what: Criteria-driven search that builds a set of entities (people or companies) matching a query, with enrichment. Matching results cost credits; non-matching results are free. Identity resolution method not described on the billing page.
why_it_matters: A search-to-set product: the way a user builds a people list from criteria, which is the front door our graph would need.
numbers: Starter $49/mo with 8,000 credits and 100 results per Webset; Pro $449/mo with 100,000 credits and 1,000 results per Webset; matching result costs 10 credits (Websets billing page). Companies: 70M+ (Explorium, third-party). No people count found.
ui_notes: Results per Webset cap by plan (100 Starter, 1,000 Pro).
note: Free-tier figures conflict between third-party sites (1,000 vs 20,000 requests). Not a people DB as such; included as a search front door. | check: Could not verify: websets.exa.ai/billing returned HTTP 429, so the $49/$449 plan prices and credit allotments are unconfirmed. Re-check when rate limit clears.

name: LittleSis
what: Free, volunteer-edited graph of people, organisations and the relationships between them (board seats, donations, employment and similar). Each relationship carries citations. Run by Public Accountability Initiative. The About page was blocked by bot protection at fetch, so the merge and review process is not verified.
why_it_matters: A relationship-first people graph where every edge has a citation. It is the closest existing model for linking people to documents, which is our book/repo/video layer.
numbers: 303,497 people; 136,225 organisations; 1,868,982 relationships; 11,403,775 citations (homepage snapshot, undated): https://littlesis.org/home . Older dev snapshot 299,685 people.
ui_notes: Public database pages; no API terms read.
note: Counts from cached pages and grow over time. Licence not verified; the about page was blocked by Anubis. | check: Could not verify: littlesis.org/database returned an Anubis bot-block page, so 303,497 people / 1,868,982 relationships are unconfirmed. Re-check from a browser or the bulk dump.

name: VIAF (Virtual International Authority File)
what: Union of national library authority files (over 50 contributors, including ISNI) into clusters, one per entity, each with a persistent numeric ID. Clusters are recomputed monthly, so IDs can merge or split. Records match on explicit identifiers, string matching, or both. Names with initials are no longer matched directly to full names after false merges. The ISNI quality team uses marker fields on corrected records to block false merges and to split clusters. Open data under ODC-BY.
why_it_matters: A mature multi-source person-merge pipeline that uses corrective marker fields and monthly re-clustering. Copy the split-marker idea and the conservative string-match rule.
numbers: Cluster and identifier counts not retrieved; the only figure found was the 2011 OCLC announcement (https://www.oclc.org/developer/news/2011/viaf-gets-bigger-and-better.en.html). Check viaf.org for current totals.
ui_notes: ISNI records carry status: assigned, provisional or suspect.
note: Guidelines PDF seen in search results and not read in full. Totals missing.

name: Scopus Author Profiles (Elsevier)
what: Author profile graph built from indexed works. Profiles are created automatically and split when an author's name, subject area, affiliation or co-authors change, so one person can have several profiles. Merges and splits are requested through the Author Feedback Wizard and reviewed by Elsevier before being applied. University guidance puts review at 1 to 2 weeks. Advice: verify by document titles and co-authors, not name similarity.
why_it_matters: A conservative-split, human-merge design. It shows the cost of splitting by default: a long review queue for users. Our queue should accept merges as well as splits.
numbers: Profile total not found. Review timelines from university guidance (third-party, approximate).
ui_notes: Feedback wizard can merge, split, remove documents and correct details.
note: Process described from secondary guides; the Elsevier page was not fully read. Count missing.

name: UK Companies House officers register
what: Statutory register of company directors and secretaries, served through a free public API. Officer lists are per company and per officer. Date of birth is published as month and year only. Licence is described as Open Government Licence v3.0 by one secondary source; a forum answer cites the CDPA s.47 database right.
why_it_matters: A legally filed, government-issued people-to-company link. It is the best source for linking a person to the companies they run, and it is free at the point of use.
numbers: Rate limit 600 requests per 5 minutes per key (secondary source, Companies House API docs). Officer total not found.
ui_notes: Requires register_view=true and register_type (e.g. directors) or the request returns 400 (forum post).
note: Official developer-specs page not fetched; rate limit and parameters come from forum and secondary sources. Licence is unconfirmed.

name: Google Knowledge Graph Search API
what: Entity lookup API over Google's Knowledge Graph, returning entities (including Person type) with entity IDs and links to Wikipedia and Wikidata. Useful as an ID crosswalk for well-known people rather than a full people database.
why_it_matters: A free key-lookup layer for notable people: resolve a name to a stable entity ID and a Wikidata link. Good as a join helper, not as a source of coverage.
numbers: Free quota up to 100,000 read calls per day per project (Google usage-limits page). Person entity count not disclosed.
ui_notes: Person type filter and fields not read in this run.
note: Entity count not disclosed. Person-type details not read.

name: S2AND: Author name disambiguation benchmark and reference model (Semantic Scholar)
what: Benchmark and evaluation system for author name disambiguation, unifying eight AND datasets into one format with a shared feature set. Ships an open-source reference model. Reports a B3 F1 near 90% against 78.4% for the production Semantic Scholar system.
why_it_matters: The best open, reproducible AND evaluation we found. It gives us a scoring harness (B3 F1) to measure our own merges against published baselines.
numbers: Average B3 F1 about 90% for S2AND vs 78.4% for Semantic Scholar production (per paper abstract snippet). Package: https://pypi.org/project/s2and/
note: Figures from search snippet; full paper not read. Licensing section on PyPI not read.

name: Mix'n'match (Wikimedia)
what: Wikimedia tool that matches external identifier catalogues (including people catalogues such as biographical dictionaries) to Wikidata items. A human confirms or rejects each candidate match, so the crosswalk grows with reviewed links rather than automatic merges.
why_it_matters: A working human-in-the-loop crosswalk engine: candidate match, one-click confirm, write back to a shared identity hub. Copy the review loop.
numbers: Catalogue count differs by page version: 2,500+ (Manual), 3,000+, 4,500+ and 5,800+ datasets (Meta-Wiki page). Not a people count. Source: https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Mix%27n%27match/Manual
ui_notes: Browser tool with match/no match/unsure decisions (Manual).
note: Catalogue counts conflict across page versions. Overlaps with held ODNB row only at the catalogue level; the matching HOW is new.

name: Crunchbase (people and founder data)
what: Company-centric database with people (founders, executives, board) in its firmographics package. API access is enterprise-licensed; a free tier was discontinued per third-party sources, and a Basic key gets 403 on the search API (PostHog connector doc). Identity linking is by Crunchbase person and org IDs; resolution method not described in sources read.
why_it_matters: The standard investor-side people graph of founders and operators. A link target for our people records, not a source we can freely pull.
numbers: Person count not found. Vendr median buyer about $20,000/yr (total spend, third-party). API pricing is quote-only.
ui_notes: Search by role, location and organisation (Jentic, third-party).
note: Official Crunchbase docs not fetched. Access terms are from third parties and may be out of date.
